ANSWER: The decision logic lives in `src/memory/guard.rs`:

- **`secret_kind(text: &str) -> Option<&'static str>`** — this is the top-level function that decides whether a piece of text looks like a credential. It first checks the text against a set of named regex patterns (`SECRETS`, e.g. patterns for known key formats), then scans for any long token (≥32 chars matching `[A-Za-z0-9+/_=-]`) and calls the helper on each match.

- **`looks_random(token: &str) -> bool`** — this is the helper that distinguishes high-entropy base64 keys from hex hashes and IDs. It requires the token to have mixed case (lowercase, uppercase, and digits), then computes a Shannon entropy over byte frequencies and returns `true` only when entropy exceeds 4.2 bits — a threshold hex/base32 can't reach but base64 keys typically exceed.

`check_secret` (also in `src/memory/guard.rs`) calls `secret_kind` and formats the refusal message; it is called from `check`, the top-level write validator that runs before any database write.

CONFIDENCE: high
